items.title: Marty Grosz interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 4, 1995
items.q: “Rhythm, Rhythm” by Lionel Hampton, with Johnny Hodges and Allan Reuss was on it and Cozy Cole and Jess Stacey and everything.

ctx.x: I’m assuming that. So I think that on the scale of things important to spend money on at a time when money was not that available, I think he probably would have thought you know, he remembered from his youth in Germany, every house had what they called the “gout de stoupa,” the good room that was like the living room that was never used. You know what I mean? And the piano was often this sacred symbol with a piano scarf on it, and don’t put this on it, don’t put that, don’t touch that, that’s the piano. I will…

piano. You know, and so forth. And maybe that’s what he thought, I don’t know. So anyway, I sort of got a guitar, I saved up my money doing errands and allowance and jobs and things like that, and I went to New York and got like a twenty dollar guitar, a terrible thing, I didn’t know any better, but I kept fiddling with it at home. And I was so embarrassed kind of that I was so lousy. You know I’d try to play along with records. Lionel Hampton I remember was one of the ones. “Rhythm, Rhythm” by Lionel Hampton,…
